/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 13 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2250 (49)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3437 (119)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1862 (7)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1320 (12)
Baltic Handysize Index: 701 (2)
CAPESIZE
The market began the week on a subdued yet positive note, with the BCI 182 5TC advancing by $1,082 to settle at $31,170. C5 rose by $0.370 to $12.390, while C3 also edged higher by $0.255 to $30.455. In the Pacific, activity was sluggish but sentiment remained positive, supported by decent volumes and the presence of two miners on C5. A notable bid-offer spread persisted throughout the day, with bids opening around $12.00 against offers in the high $12s, and no fixtures reported at the time of writing. There were rumours of $12.90 and $12.60 being concluded, though nothing confirmed. A similar dynamic was observed on C3, where bids were said to be creeping towards $30.50, while offers remained closer to $32, highlighting a degree of hesitation from both sides. The Atlantic basin was comparatively quiet but maintained a positive undertone, with South Brazil and West Africa to China routes described as well supported.
PANAMAX
Today we experienced a more reserved start to the week with fundamentals in the Atlantic looking unaltered from the previous week as the cargo and tonnage list look well matched. Sentiment leaned on the more positive side with the P1A rising by $214 to $13,155. In Asia, cargoes into China remain evident with improved numbers being discussed for tonnage available within April. The P5TC increased by $61 to conclude at $16,757.

Atlantic
Cobelfret were said to have covered their stem from Kamsar into San Ciprian for 21/27 April dates, but further information lacked. Messrs Geneva Bulkers were talked to be on subjects for their East Coast South America 21 April stem back to the Continent, but other details were limited.

Asia
The Shine Crystal (82,242 2025) open in Zhanjiang 15/16 April was said to have fixed for a trip via Australia to India. The Shen Hua 801 (75,331 2013) open in Zhangzhou 14/15 April was said to have fixed a round voyage via Indonesia at $16,000 but the charterer was unknown. Messrs Oldendorff were said to have taken the Jag Aalok (82,022 2016) open in Chiba 13/14 April for a North Pacific petcoke run. The scrubber fitted Basic Star (81,947 2024) open Nanao 19/22 April was reported fixed.
SUPRAMAX
With some still off due to the Orthodox holiday, it was rather a slow start to the week. Having said that sentiment remained positive in most areas, although as per usual there was a bit of a standoff between owners' and charterer's expectations’ US Gulf remained firm again brokers saying demand remained both for fronthaul and trans Atlantic. Some felt better levels of enquiry were being seen from the South Atlantic. Similar from Asia, sentiment remained in positive territory. The 11TC average closed up $143
at $16,681.

Atlantic
The CMB Teniers (63,667 2021) was heard to have fixed basis delivery Santos end April trip Far East at $17,500 + $750,000 ballast bonus with Reachy.

Asia
The Vosco Jubilant (57,903 2014) Singapore was reported fixed for a trip via Indonesia redelivery Thailand at $18,000 with Oldendorff.

HANDYSIZE
The market opened the week on a generally positive note, with some regions holding steady while others posted modest gains, although fresh information remained limited. The BHSI edged up by 2 points to 701, while the 7TC average rose by $53 to $12,626. The Continent and Mediterranean saw relatively limited activity, with some fresh demand and tonnage entering the market, though bid/offer levels were reported below those seen last week. The US Gulf appeared to stabilise, with fundamentals becoming more balanced and only limited fluctuations observed. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic experienced a quiet session, with sources describing cautious activity as a wide bid/offer spread persisted, alongside a few positional fixtures being rumoured. In the Pacific, the week began on a subdued note, with fundamentals largely unchanged. Rate levels remained mostly flat.

Market Fundamentals
US-Iran Talks Stall, Oil Spikes

Weekend negotiations between the US and Iran in Islamabad concluded without agreement after extended discussions, with key differences persisting over Iran’s nuclear programme and Strait of Hormuz oversight, newswires report. Oil markets reacted sharply, with Brent crude rising ~8% to $102.8/bbl as of 13 April amid fears of potential supply disruption and escalation risks.

Chinese Iron Ore Stockpiles

In the week to 10 April, Chinese iron ore stockpiles eased 0.7 Mt to 169.0 Mt, according to 42 portside locations monitored by Umetal. Meanwhile, inventories stood 26.6 Mt above the same time last year.

India Defers Planned Maintenance of Coal Facilities

India has deferred planned maintenance shutdowns at 10,000 MW of coal-fired power plants to ensure high electricity demand during the summer months is met, as the Middle East war has squeezed access to liquefied natural gas. The government has asked two-thirds of the scheduled plants to defer maintenance until July, when monsoon rains are expected to lift hydro power generation. Gas-based capacity accounts for just 1.4% of India’s overall power requirement, but shortages can add pressure to a grid already strained by booming demand.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve accelerated on the upside in response to a firmer physical market, together with uncertainty surrounding the situation on the middle-east. The May and June contract were the biggest gainers with pays up to 31750 and 31950 respectively, as the May v Jun spread narrowed and strengthened up to -400. The Apr was less supported, trading between 28000 and 28750. Liquidity on the Q2 was surprisingly thin, reaching a high of 30900, while Q3 was actively trading within a range of 29000-29750. The Q3 v Q4 spread narrowed up to flat, as the Q4 was paid to a high of 29850. Cal27 dominated volumes trading 25250 early on, then up to a ceiling of 25500.

PMX
PMX opened flat in the morning and carried that through into the afternoon, with participants remaining tentative due to ongoing political uncertainty and some of the lowest volume seen this year. Apr traded at a low of 17100 and was hit up to 17350, while May moved between 18750 and 19150. Jun traded between18950 to 19400 before closing around 19200, with Q2 bouncing around 18350 to 18600 and closing near 18400, Q3 went from 18600 down to 18450, while Q4 traded around 17100. On the back end, Cal 27 traded around 14800, falling around 100 dollars on the day, with Cal 28 printing 13900 and Cal 29 around 13700. Overall, it was a very quiet session with low participation and a largely flat tone across the curve.

SMX + HANDY
Limited liquidity in the SMX market to start, as the curve gapped higher on open, though support slowly eased and the curve drifted lower over the day. Trading was concentrated to the front of the curve trading outright and against the PMX, as Apr traded from 15600 – 15150, May 17000 – 16600, Jun 17000 – 16900 and Q2 at 16200. Q3 traded relatively actively from 16600 – 16300. Handy May traded 15250 and Q4 13600 – 13500.

Carbon
EU carbon futures closed slightly lower, down 0.3% on the Dec26 contract at �72.62/eua. While energy prices increased following news that the U.S. would blockade some cargoes through the Strait of Hormuz, the fact is that actual energy consumption in Europe, and resulting carbon emissions, are more likely to decline due to a combination of higher energy prices and potential supply shortages.

The futures market was also pressured by today's EU Common auction, which cleared 2.7m allowances at �70.62/eua. While this was roughly in line with the same auction last Thursday, it was also below daily spot futures values.

Market Fundamentals
US-Iran Talks Stall, Oil Spikes
Weekend negotiations between the US and Iran in
Islamabad concluded without agreement after extended
discussions, with key diﬀerences persisting over Iran’s
nuclear programme and Strait of Hormuz oversight,
newswires report. Oil markets reacted sharply, with Brent
crude rising ~8% to $102.8/bbl as of 13 April amid fears of
potential supply disruption and escalation risks.
Chinese Iron Ore Stockpiles
In the week to 10 April, Chinese iron ore stockpiles eased 0.7
Mt to 169.0 Mt, according to 42 portside locations monitored
by Umetal. Meanwhile, inventories stood 26.6 Mt above the
same time last year.
India Defers Planned Maintenance of Coal Facilities
India has deferred planned maintenance shutdowns at
10,000 MW of coal-ﬁred power plants to ensure high
electricity demand during the summer months is met, as the
Middle East war has squeezed access to liqueﬁed natural
gas. The government has asked two-thirds of the scheduled
plants to defer maintenance until July, when monsoon rains
are expected to lift hydro power generation. Gas-based
capacity accounts for just 1.4% of India’s overall power
requirement, but shortages can add pressure to a grid
already strained by booming demand.
Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve accelerated on the upside in response to
a ﬁrmer physical market, together with uncertainty
surrounding the situation on the middle-east. The May and
June contract were the biggest gainers with pays up to 31750
and 31950 respectively, as the May v Jun spread narrowed
and strengthened up to -400. The Apr was less supported,
trading between 28000 and 28750. Liquidity on the Q2 was
surprisingly thin, reaching a high of 30900, while Q3 was
actively trading within a range of 29000-29750. The Q3 v Q4
spread narrowed up to ﬂat, as the Q4 was paid to a high of
29850. Cal27 dominated volumes trading 25250 early on,
then up to a ceiling of 25500.
PMX
PMX opened ﬂat in the morning and carried that through
into the afternoon, with participants remaining tentative due
to ongoing political uncertainty and some of the lowest
volume seen this year. Apr traded at a low of 17100 and was
hit up to 17350, while May moved between 18750 and 19150.
Jun traded between18950 to 19400 before closing around
19200, with Q2 bouncing around 18350 to 18600 and closing
near 18400, Q3 went from 18600 down to 18450, while Q4
traded around 17100. On the back end, Cal 27 traded around
14800, falling around 100 dollars on the day, with Cal 28
printing 13900 and Cal 29 around 13700. Overall, it was a
very quiet session with low participation and a largely ﬂat
tone across the curve.
SMX + HANDY
Limited liquidity in the SMX market to start, as the curve
gapped higher on open, though support slowly eased and
the curve drifted lower over the day. Trading was
concentrated to the front of the curve trading outright and
against the PMX, as Apr traded from 15600 – 15150, May
17000 – 16600, Jun 17000 – 16900 and Q2 at 16200. Q3Cape 180 5TC

Carbon
EU carbon futures closed slightly lower, down 0.3% on the
Dec26 contract at €72.62/eua. While energy prices increased
following news that the U.S. would blockade some cargoes
through the Strait of Hormuz, the fact is that actual energy
consumption in Europe, and resulting carbon emissions, are
more likely to decline due to a combination of higher energy
prices and potential supply shortages.
The futures market was also pressured by today's EU
Common auction, which cleared 2.7m allowances at
€70.62/eua. While this was roughly in line with the same
auction last Thursday, it was also below daily spot futures

items.parsed_text: 13th April 2026 Iron Ore TSI 62%: - - TSI Premium Coking Coal: - - Brent UK Oil: 99.95 4.75 EUA: 71.21 -0.26 BDI 2,250 49 BCI 180 3,437 119 BPI 1,862 7 BSI 1,320 12 BHSI 701 2 Market Fundamentals US-Iran Talks Stall, Oil Spikes Weekend negotiations between the US and Iran in Islamabad concluded without agreement after extended discussions, with key differences persisting over Iran’s nuclear programme and Strait of Hormuz oversight, newswires report. Oil markets reacted sharply, with Brent crude rising ~8% to $102.8/bbl as of 13 April amid fears of potential supply disruption and escalation risks. Chinese Iron Ore Stockpiles In the week to 10 April, Chinese iron ore stockpiles eased 0.7 Mt to 169.0 Mt, according to 42 portside locations monitored by Umetal. Meanwhile, inventories stood 26.6 Mt above the same time last year. India Defers Planned Maintenance of Coal Facilities India has deferred planned maintenance shutdowns at 10,000 MW of coal-fired power plants to ensure high electricity demand during the summer months is met, as the Middle East war has squeezed access to liquefied natural gas. The government has asked two-thirds of the scheduled plants to defer maintenance until July, when monsoon rains are expected to lift hydro power generation. Gas-based capacity accounts for just 1.4% of India’s overall power requirement, but shortages can add pressure to a grid already strained by booming demand. Trading Commentary Cape The Cape FFA curve accelerated on the upside in response to a firmer physical market, together with uncertainty surrounding the situation on the middle-east. The May and June contract were the biggest gainers with pays up to 31750 and 31950 respectively, as the May v Jun spread narrowed and strengthened up to -400. The Apr was less supported, trading between 28000 and 28750. Liquidity on the Q2 was surprisingly thin, reaching a high of 30900, while Q3 was actively trading within a range of 29000-29750. The Q3 v Q4 spread narrowed up to flat, as the Q4 was paid to a high of 29850. Cal27 dominated volumes trading 25250 early on, then up to a ceiling of 25500. PMX PMX opened flat in the morning and carried that through into the afternoon, with participants remaining tentative due to ongoing political uncertainty and some of the lowest volume seen this year. Apr traded at a low of 17100 and was hit up to 17350, while May moved between 18750 and 19150. Jun traded between18950 to 19400 before closing around 19200, with Q2 bouncing around 18350 to 18600 and closing near 18400, Q3 went from 18600 down to 18450, while Q4 traded around 17100. On the back end, Cal 27 traded around 14800, falling around 100 dollars on the day, with Cal 28 printing 13900 and Cal 29 around 13700. Overall, it was a very quiet session with low participation and a largely flat tone across the curve. SMX + HANDY Limited liquidity in the SMX market to start, as the curve gapped higher on open, though support slowly eased and the curve drifted lower over the day. Trading was concentrated to the front of the curve trading outright and against the PMX, as Apr traded from 15600 – 15150, May 17000 – 16600, Jun 17000 – 16900 and Q2 at 16200.
